The Worker-only HTTP kernel. `http.js`: `HttpError` (with `HttpError.of(code, message?, headers?, details?)`), `json`, `apiError`, `redirect`, `requireMethod`, `requireSameOrigin`, `requireMutationOwner`, `requireReadOwnerIfPresent`, `readBounded`, `readJSON`, `tickerParam`, `requireTicker`, `keepAlive`, `errorText`, `internalKey(namespace, path)` (the `https://flows-<namespace>.internal/<path>` Cache API keys) and `edgeCache` (`handle`, `get`, `put`, each failure a miss). `errors.js`: `ERRORS`, one frozen `[status, default message]` per code. `log.js`: `logFailure(level, message, fields, error)`, the one shape of an unexpected-failure log. `server/` holds no top-level mutable binding, no comments and is excluded from the static bundle. The suite runs every helper against a verbatim copy of the helper it replaced over tables of requests, bodies, origins and tickers, holds every literal `new HttpError(status, "code"` in `worker.js` and `shared/` to the table's status, and holds the failure-log key order. Literal `new HttpError(` sites stay where they are (the ingest scans pin some); a module moves to `HttpError.of` with its own move.

The Worker's route table, consulted first by `route()` and falling through to the remaining `if` chain. `createRouter(...families)` validates each row `{ id, path, methods, auth, handler }` (an absolute path and an id declared once, a non-empty list of HTTP methods, `auth` of `none` or `flows`, a handler), freezes it, and `handle(rc, gates)` returns `null` for a path with no row, else runs the method gate, then the session gate (`gates.flows`, a missing session being the 401 `unauthorized`), then the handler with `{ request, env, url, ctx, session }`: the order the Flows prefix block always had. `flowsReadRows(deps)` is the first family, 23 `GET` rows behind the Flows session: `board`, `brief`, `card`, `card-x`, `hist`, the overlaid `flowalerts`, `pulse` and `news`, and the fifteen plain nightly reads built by one `nightly(key, pending)` factory (`market`, `events`, `scoretrack`, `meta`, `political`, `unusual`, `movers`, `sectors`, `sector-premium`, `universe`, `regime`, `ideas`, `focus`, `roster`, `record`). The worker-local readers it needs (`readServed`, `readFlowsPayload`, `readWithOverlay`, `passthrough`, `recallLastGood`, `storeGone`, `absentKey`, `cardWithEngine`, `briefWithLive`, `nightlyFreshHeaders`) are injected, so `server/` imports nothing from `worker.js` or `cloudflare:`. A new route in this family is a row, never a new `if`; the ceiling enumeration in `flows-reads-contract` takes the table's paths plus the literals still in the chain (at least thirty together) and fails for any without a rows-read ceiling. The suite runs every row against a verbatim copy of the branch it replaced over eight stored-row worlds and seven store behaviours, comparing status, headers, body, errors and the order of calls.

The flows-desk family in the route table: `flowsDeskRows(deps)` is three `GET` rows behind the Flows session, `chain` (keyed by ticker, strategy and rank, 120 rows), `strategy` (the context, or one expiry with or without the engine; a malformed expiry is `400 invalid_expiry` before any gate) and `live` (the stock-state quote). Each handler builds the member's `vendorGate` once and hands the Worker's single-flight `serveCachedVendorRead` (or `quoteResponse`) its key, gate and builder; the builders, the gate and the reader are injected and stay in `worker.js`, so the family names no limiter and makes no vendor call itself. `EXPIRY_RE` and `RANK_KEYS` are read by the handlers, not the Worker. The suite runs every row against a verbatim copy of the branch it replaced over the parameter grid (tickers, strategies, ranks, expiries, engine and refresh flags, two members), comparing status, headers, body, errors and the order of calls, and holds the 405-before-401 gate order. `tape`, `now` and `lk` stay in the chain for the live-layer family.

The flows-ai family in the route table: `flowsAiRows(deps)` is four rows behind the Flows session, `ai-usage`, `summary` and `dossier` by `GET` and `ask` by `POST`. The handlers are the route bodies only: the board summary or a `summaryResponse` for a ticker (a malformed ticker is `400 invalid_ticker`), the dossier behind `ensureFlowsTables`, and the Ask box (same-origin check, the question, the `AI_ASK` flood brake with its `Retry-After`, the stored briefing with its live overlay, then `askAnswer`). Everything that reaches a model stays in `worker.js` behind `cappedAi` and `meteredAi` and is injected (`askSpend`, `summaryResponse`, `readFlowsSummary`, `neuronProvenance`, `dossierResponse`, `askQuestion`, `askAnswer`, `readFlowsPayload`, `briefWithLive`, and `ASK_FLOOD_PERIOD_S`, which the contract reads off the Worker); the module names no model binding, and `checkModelCalls` still reads it as part of `server/`. The prefix block's method gate is `GET` alone now that `ask` is a `POST` row. The suite runs every row against a verbatim copy of the branch it replaced over the parameter grid (tickers, board summaries, stored briefings, origins, limiter behaviours, three callers) and holds the 405-before-401 gate order.

The AI broker and its outcome telemetry. `shared/flows-ai-broker.js` is pure: the four surfaces (`board`, `neuron`, `ask`, `read`), the fourteen outcomes (`clean`, `trimmed`, `refused`, `unparsable`, `overlong`, `empty`, `length`, `budget`, `class`, `user`, `allowance`, `capacity`, `plan`, `unreachable`), `chainFor`, `transportOutcome` (a reply with no text), `guardOutcome` (the stored `llm` and `guard` of a surface mapped to an outcome and a low-cardinality reason), `tokenOf` (a culprit, 40 characters, no control or bidi characters) and `foldCounters` (the owner block's shape: per surface and model, calls, outcomes, the share of calls that reached a model whose wording failed, mean and max latency, and the fifty latest refusals). `server/ai.js` is the I/O: `aiCall(env, deps, { surface, chain, messages, opts, onUsage })` runs `askModels(deps.ai(), ...)`, times it, settles a reply with no text itself and returns the reply with `call.settle(verdict, culprit)` for the surface to call once it has judged the wording (a second settle does nothing). A settle upserts one `flows_ai_outcome` row (day, surface, model, outcome, reason: `n`, `ms_sum`, `ms_max`) and, for a wording failure with a culprit, writes `flows_ai_reject (surface, slot 0..49)` in the same batch; it never throws, and a store that refuses it is logged once (`ai outcome not recorded`). `readAiBlock(env, deps, { days })` is the owner block in one trip (today's counters; up to seven days behind `days`) and `pruneAiOutcomes` keeps eight days, run in the 03:00 ET window. The block is mounted by the health and owner-view row (P1-27). Nothing in it reads the binding or runs a model: `shared/flows-ai.js` stays the only place. The suite covers the outcome table, the fold, `aiCall` against a scripted binding and a counting D1 (one trip a call, two rows for a refusal with a culprit, a ring that wraps at fifty, a refused or missing store, the budget refusal counted without the model asked), the block's trips and rows, retention, the registry and migration 0017 parity, and the scans.

The flows-ingest family, the store and the schema registry. `flowsIngestRows(deps)` is one row, `/api/flows/ingest` by `GET`, `POST` and `DELETE`, whose credential is its own bearer token (the nightly, the static live token on a loopback host, or the live OIDC token) and not the Flows session; the method gate, the credential checks and the key and scope rules run in the order the branch had them. `server/store.js` is the only module that holds `flows_payload` SQL: `createFlowsStore({ ensureFlowsTables })` has `read`, `metadata`, `listing`, `remove`, `createArchive` and `write` (the nightly's `meta` lands its ledger row in the same batch), and exports `storedFrom`, `ingestKeyParts`, `INGEST_VIEW_KEY_RE` and the listing limits; `worker.js` reads the nightly rows through the same store. `server/schema.js` is the registry of the Flows statements, `{ name, table, ddl, addedColumns, migration, owner }`: the twelve the Worker has always sent (built from the DDL each domain exports plus the six tables that were literals in `worker.js`, in the order it sent them) and `flows_ai_outcome` and `flows_ai_reject` after them; `FLOWS_SCHEMA_SQL` is derived from it. `upgradeColumns(db, table, added, known?)` replaces `upgradeClockColumns` for every table: it adds only the columns a table lacks, tolerates `duplicate column`, rethrows anything else, and takes names and types only in the shapes `checkAdded` allows. `applySchema(db, registry)` is the bootstrap `ensureFlowsTables` runs: one batch of the CREATEs and one `PRAGMA table_info` per table that has added columns (today `flows_clock` alone, so fifteen statements), then the upgrades. A new column on a registered table is one entry in its `addedColumns` list (`CLOCK_ADDED_COLUMNS`, `LEDGER_ADDED_COLUMNS`, which is empty today) plus the same column in the table's DDL, `schema.sql` and a migration, and it is added at first use instead of being refused by `batchWithLedger`. The suite runs the row against a verbatim copy of the branch it replaced over 7 credentials, 6 methods, 39 queries and 5 bodies (statements, call order, errors, bodies and the rows left behind), checks the store, the registry against the migrations and `schema.sql` (fourteen statements), `upgradeColumns` against hostile names, races and refused batches, and the Worker scans.

The Worker's whole routing surface in process, with no server: every route literal and prefix family, as anonymous, Flows member, Flows owner and Lab user, under six methods (plus the rail with `PULSE` absent, the switch off and the rail on, and cross-origin and owner-mismatch mutations), on a pinned clock, a fake `ASSETS`, a refusing `fetch` and `tests/lib/d1-fake.mjs`. Status, `Allow`, `Content-Type`, `Cache-Control`, `Location`, `error.code`, the seven security headers, the `X-Fresh-*` set and the cookie names are compared with the snapshot; a behaviour change regenerates it with `node route-matrix.mjs --write` in a pull request that moves no code. The fake D1 cannot return `RETURNING` rows, so the `DELETE /api/progress` cell is a 500 on the fake only. It also holds `worker.js` to one top-level `const state = createState()` and no other top-level mutable state, and `server/` (when it exists) to none.

The nightly's pinned dry-run clock and the golden emit. `FLOWS_DRY_NOW` (an ISO instant ending in `Z`, honoured only with `--dry-run`, anything else throws) pins `stampNow()`/`stampDate()`, the one clock every payload stamp (`generatedAt`, `readAt`, `screenerReadAt`, `refreshedAt`) is read from; elapsed-time and deadline measures keep the wall clock, and the pipeline's own source scan fails on a bare `new Date().toISOString()`. `nightlyEmit()` builds the dry-run emit once (CI default clock `2026-08-24T21:45:00Z`) into `FLOWS_EMIT_DIR`, which `tests/run.mjs` sets to one directory per runner invocation and removes at the end, or into a temporary directory of its own; a mark holding a fingerprint of `scripts/` and `shared/` makes a stale directory rebuild. The eight emit consumers (`flows-card-render`, `flows-events-contract`, `flows-overlay-contract`, `flows-payload-shape`, `flows-positioning-contract`, `flows-strip`, `flows-ticker-contract`, `flows-unusual-contract`) read it instead of running their own. The golden suite (the first half of `test:pipeline`) hashes every emitted payload against the manifest, builds a second emit to prove two runs at one clock are byte-identical, and names the payload and top-level keys that moved; `node flows-pipeline-golden.mjs --write` regenerates the manifest after an intended change and `--against <emit dir of the old tree>` prints the leaf paths.

The statistics leaf: no imports, no clock, no randomness beyond the seeded `mulberry32`. Mean, sample variance and deviation, median, quantiles, share at or below, average-rank percentile, Pearson and Spearman, the Wilson interval, effective n under clustering, the t critical value and the mean interval, the Newey-West standard error, a seeded stationary bootstrap and its interval, Brier, log score, the reliability table with the Murphy decomposition (reliability - resolution + uncertainty + within-bin variance - 2 x within-bin covariance, exact for binned forecasts), Benjamini-Hochberg. A null never becomes a zero: an empty or non-numeric input answers `null`. `gen-stats-fixtures.py` (scipy, numpy, statsmodels; the versions and the generator's SHA-256 are in the fixture) writes the committed JSON the contract reads without Python. Consumers: `shared/flows-vol.js`, `shared/flows-features.js`, `shared/flows-cross.js`, and the medians of `shared/flows-political.js`, `flows-premium.js`, `flows-dossier.js`, `flows-variation.js`, `flows-market.js` and `scripts/flows-quant-pipeline.mjs`.

The one news row and the one vendor-rows reader. `newsFields(row)` is the nightly's `news` row (headline, source, createdAt, createdAtMs, major, sentiment, tickers, tags; null without a headline) and `newsRow(row, at)` is the same fields behind the rail's `id` and `ts`, so the nightly and the `nw` topic cannot drift. `rowsOf(body, key = "data")` (array or empty) is the reader behind `shared/flows-live.js`, the legs' `common.mjs` and the pulse's and political feed's `unwrapRows`; `rowsOrNull` (array or null) is `shared/flows-vol.js`'s and the default of `shared/flows-positioning.js`'s.

The nightly. The entry is the command line: the session prelude and the unranked-refresh early return, `runLiveMode`, `main` (one `ctx`, eleven awaited sections), and a re-export of every name the suites import, so no suite imports a module path. The modules sit in layers and an import may only point down: `flags` (the process flags and the `FLOWS_DRY_NOW` pin), `vendor-params` (what is asked of the vendor and the call budget), `vendor` (`uw`, the permit queue, the read pace and the pool), `store` (ingest URL, the live credential, read, publish, retire, prune and the dated-key grammar), `clock`, `rank` (scoring and shaping, `enrich`), `fixtures` (the dry run's synthetic vendor), `archive` (board memory, the dated walk, the record's inputs, the roster ledger), then the sections, `runUniverse` to `runClose` (`runCompute` between `runFocus` and `runClose`), none importing another; `stages` is a leaf. A section destructures what it reads from `ctx` and returns what a later one needs with `Object.assign(ctx, ...)`; `tests/flows-legs-contract.mjs` holds each declaration to its module, the layer rule and the no-comment rule for the whole tree. A test reads the nightly through `nightlySource()` (entry, then every module, each marked), `nightlySlice()` (throws when a slice crosses a module) or `nightlyExecution()` (the entry with each section spliced in where it runs) from `tests/lib/source-scan.mjs`, never by reading one file.

The nightly's stage table (`STAGES`: id, fatal or isolated, `needs`, declared `publishes`) and `createStageRunner`: `step(id)` for a fatal stage, `run(id, work, onError)` for an isolated one (the failure is recorded and handed to `onError`, a fatal one rethrows), `skip`, `note(key)` from `publish`, `detail(fields)` (at most six extra numbers or short strings on the open stage's record, never a record field), `finish`, `records()`; given a `cpu` clock the runner adds `cpu` (whole milliseconds of the process's CPU time) to every record, and the dry run pins that clock to 0 with the stamp. `meta` is the last write of the nightly, after the health gate, and carries `stages` and `health` (`healthRecord`); `publishedStore.meta` is set earlier so the brief still reads it. The pipeline's pipeline-contract block holds the table to the source (every id once, in order, fatal stages stepped and isolated ones run) and to the dry run (every key declared, `meta` last).

The compute stage, an isolated stage after `card-x` and before `roster`, once the vendor reads are done: it imports no vendor client, store or archive, so it cannot call the vendor or publish. `computeNames` runs the registered `COMPUTE_JOBS` (frozen, empty until a model brings one: `{ id, run(ticker, ctx) }`) over the carded names one at a time with a turn of the event loop between names; a name that spends more than `COMPUTE_NAME_CPU_MS` (1,000) of CPU is named in `over`, the stage stops before the next name once its share (names times that budget) is spent or the run's deadline has passed, and a job that throws costs that name that job only. Values are kept by job and ticker on `ctx.computed` for a later stage to publish. The stage record carries `cpu`, `names`, `jobs`, `over`, `failed` and `stopped`.

Does conviction order outcomes (P2-22): a pure leaf over `flows-record.js`'s forward-close rule that scores each archived board name as a hit when it beat the session's equal-weight board average in its board's direction, fits `logit P(hit) = a + b·cnv/100` with a session-clustered sandwich and Student t on G-1 degrees of freedom, reads terciles of `cnv` with Wilson intervals on the effective count, the clustered top-minus-bottom gap and its minimum detectable size (2.8 standard errors), the pooled Spearman with a leave-one-session-out jackknife, and breadth's own coefficient. `evaluateConviction` returns `keep` (slope interval above zero and rising terciles), `relabel` (the number is an "Agreement index") or `pending` (under 60 scored sessions and 600 rows at the ten-session horizon, or no fit), published as `record.conviction`. The contract holds the estimators to numpy and scipy on 500 committed reference rows (`gen-conviction-fixtures.py` writes the JSON) and to simulated boards with a known slope; the render suite is the History page's module in Chromium against stubbed `/api/flows/record`.

The tree's shape, in about a second with no server: no import cycle over static and literal dynamic imports from `worker.js` and every script, the layer table (`shared/` imports `shared/` only, `scripts/` never `server/`, `cloudflare:*` only in `worker.js`, `assets/js` imports nothing), the declared leaves, no comment in any tracked JavaScript, CSS, HTML (inline script and style too), SQL, YAML, TOML, Python or ignore file (`docs/` excluded), and the browser floor table (Flows Safari 17 / Chrome 114 / Firefox 125, Lab and articles Safari 16.4 / Chrome 111 / Firefox 113): a feature above a surface's floor must be guarded in the window around it (`?.(`, `typeof`, `"x" in`, `&&`), and the table lists the Popover API at 17 and lookbehind at 16.4. The landing index ticker: the Worker's Yahoo parse (the change is against the previous session's close taken from the same response's dated bars, never `chartPreviousClose`; each quote keeps its own `asOf`, `asOfDay`, `prevClose`, `prevDay` and, when the response names the session of the quote's own day, `sessionEnd`) and the strip that prints each quote's own İstanbul time, `Close <weekday>` for a closed market (a close is a quote struck within five minutes of the exchange's `sessionEnd`; the lag of the quote behind the fetch decides only where there is none), and a dash for a quote with no base.

The Premium desk's client alone: its pure functions (the frontier against a brute-force Pareto set, balance parsing, tenor buckets, cent sizing, net delta) in a Node `vm`, and the page in Chromium against payload fixtures built to the chain contract (basis, time-value yield, tooltips, banners); no server.

The desk's Win % (implied) against an independent reference: `gen-desk-lab.py` (mpmath at 40 digits) prices skewed SVI chains and takes the risk-neutral probability of profit by Breeden-Litzenberger, and the suite proves the page, given the card's smile expiries, lands within 0.5pp of it and of the strategy lab on every line, while the flat fit it replaced misses by 2.5pp; the carry and the smile each line was priced on are read back from its disclosure. Chromium against `page.route` stubs, no server.
The Yahoo parse against dated five-day responses (weekend, Tokyo morning, null trailing bar, no timestamps) and the strip rendered in Chromium with a fixed clock; neither starts a server.

The landing page's motion in Chromium with no server: under reduced motion the particle field draws one still frame (eight passes, as bright as the settled trail the old loop built; a single pass measures 0.56 of it), draws it once at load and once per viewport change, redraws it at the device scale after a context restore, and fires no animation frame after the first second; the marquee's Pause button (WCAG 2.2.2) is reached by Tab, toggled by Enter, Space and a click whether or not it keeps focus, holds after focus leaves, and stays under reduced motion because the prices still auto-update; a refresh that lands while paused is held until Play in both views, a Pause and Play with nothing held leaves the bar and its focused control in place, and a refresh while playing renders at once; the bar stays below the footer at 320, 390 and 1280 px.
The Eastern clock (arithmetic, proven equal to the IANA zone), market phases, the freshness threshold table, `X-Fresh-*` headers, and the live clock's due-tests.

The per-day session ledger: the `flows_ledger` DDL, the statement builders the Tier 1 tick, the focus tick, the heartbeat write and the nightly's `meta` write append to a batch they already issue, the gap limits (the stale lines of `FRESH_CLASSES`), the view served as `ledger` on the ingest `clock` key, and the worst-key lapse the Tier 1 tick reads from the live rows.

The live layer's key registry and pure builders; the Worker's Tier 1 tick, dispatch, watchdog, live ingest, `/api/flows/lk`, `/now`, `/tape` and read-time overlays. A strip row ends in `qa`, the vendor's `quote_time` as seconds behind the read, and the key's `ahead { n, maxS }` counts the stamps that run later than the read; `priorCloseBase` and `shapeStrips` fill a null `prev_close` from the last dated nightly close and say so in `prevFill`, and hold out a row the vendor dates before the session as an all-null row (DEPLOY.md 10.5i).

The live credential: the GitHub OIDC claim policy (this repository by id, `flows-live.yml` on main), the pure JWT verifier the Worker runs, and the runner-side token request the `--live` leg uses. No shared secret.

The Actions `--live` leg (Tier 2, `live:*` keys only) and its fake vendor for `--dry-run`. `runLiveLoop` keeps the loop alive between sessions when handed a `watch`, and `chainDispatch` sends any workflow_dispatch with the job's own token.

The loop's mutual witness (Tier 1 older than 25 minutes, `live:breadth` older than 45, the nightly not landed by 21:00 ET, a broken chain, a blind ingest door; one deduplicated GitHub Issue per check, written and adopted only as `github-actions[bot]`, closed after three healthy ticks and reopened on a flap), the 17:30 ET nightly dispatch with the job's own token (a permanent refusal capped at four calls, a transient one retried every half hour to 20:30 ET), and the per-tick composition of the two over the OIDC ingest door.
A fake GitHub API and a fake Worker world on a virtual clock, and the eight dry days `--live --dry-run` runs through them.

The premium desk's basis: the vendor's `{data:{...}}` stock-state envelope, a spot that is only a regular-session price (`printOf`: the live print in the regular session, else the newest regular close), and the coherence gate between that spot and the chain (`coherence`: impossible asks, the strike bracket the `maybe_otm_only` request guarantees, one underlying fitted to the nearest expiries, a rebase past 0.25% or a refusal when the fit is too thin). The contract runs the Worker route in Node against a stubbed vendor. The desk's `asOf` is the New York date of the READ and `days` count from it; `UW_NOW` (an ISO instant, honoured only while `UW_BASE` redirects the vendor away from production) pins that read clock so the workerd suites' dated fixtures stay valid.

The pure leaf every vendor client reads: `vendorBaseInfo` and `vendorBase` accept `UW_BASE` only as the production origin, `http(s)` loopback (`127.0.0.1`, `localhost`) or an `http(s)` `*.test` host with no credentials, path, query or fragment, and otherwise answer the production origin with status `invalid`; `vendorRedirected` is true only for a loopback or `.test` base and is what unlocks the test-only `UW_NOW` and `FLOWS_RT_SCALE`; `vendorUrl`, `unwrap` (the vendor's `{data}` envelope), `classifyStatus` (`http_429`, `http_5xx`, `http_4xx`) and `retryAfterMs`. `uwFetch` in `worker.js` and the rail's REST adapter use it; the pipeline and the legs still read `FLOWS_UW_BASE_URL` directly. The allowed and refused base table is in `flows-rt-contract`, the Worker half in `flows-basis-contract`.

The premium desk's ranking: gates, annualization, the strike divisor and `rankChain`. Its mid implied volatility inverts against a per-expiry forward (`forwardPlan`): the chain's own put-call parity over up to ten near-the-money two-sided pairs (mid of at least 0.05, spread under half the mid) when there are three or more, else the card's implied carry (`deskCarry`: grade 2 or better, and only when `coherence` returned `ok`), else the rate alone. A parity forward or a carry whose log gap from the rate forward exceeds `forwardGapLimit(years)` (2% plus 0.5 a year, capped at 15%) is not believed. A rebased chain takes no carry because its fitted spot has already absorbed the carry over the fit horizon, the nearest expiries, only: later expiries of a rebased chain keep the rate-only forward unless parity places them, so their mid IV stays biased (about 1.1 vol points at 180 days and 2.1 at 360 days at a 3% carry on an out-of-the-money-only chain), a limit pinned in `tests/flows-basis-contract.mjs`. `rankChain` returns the choice per expiry as `forwards` (an empty list on a `mismatch` payload).

The home page's focus roster (Gold, Silver and Copper groups, the Mag 7, the metal funds and miners) and the NASDAQ-10 derivation from QQQ holdings. A leaf module: it imports nothing, so the Worker, the pipeline and the live leg can all read it without a cycle.

The vendor socket probe, dispatch only: handshake three ways, one connection per channel, concurrent connections, joins per connection, lag against each frame's own stamp. It prints key names and statistics, never payload values or the token. The contract runs it against a fake vendor that speaks the WebSocket protocol by hand.

The dealer gamma profile (`gammaProfile`): a leaf with no imports. Per contract it precomputes `1/(sigma sqrt(T))`, the affine part of d1 in ln x and the signed weight, so each grid point is one logarithm and one exponential per contract instead of a full set of Black-Scholes greeks; output equals the greeks-based profile to 1e-12 of the profile's peak and the flip to 1e-9, at about a tenth of the CPU (`tests/flows-quant.mjs` holds the equality against a reference copy and the CPU ratio through `tests/lib/cpu-budget.mjs`).

`screenReading`: a Neuron reading from a universe row alone, for a name with no card. A leaf that imports the consolidated state table (`STATE_LINES`, `structuresForState` in `flows-neuron.js`), `BUCKET_LINES` and `sessionsBetween`, and is imported by no module that imports it back. Facts are graded 0 or 1 and each prints its unit; a null input is withheld under its own key with its reason; dealer delta and vanna are the vendor's numbers with no direction claimed, charm a sign only at grade 0. The flow network, attached as `FlowsUI.net` (`model`, `mount`, `of`) and loaded only by the unusual page, whose hero it is. `model(rows, o)` is pure: each flagged window's premium is split by the vendor's ask-side and bid-side attribution (the rest, left between the quotes or never split, is Unattributed) and routed side, sector (the nightly universe's; the top five and Other once there are more than six), name (the largest ten, fewer on a narrow screen, and Other names), then lean (calls at ask and puts at bid bullish, calls at bid and puts at ask bearish, by convention) or expiry horizon (calendar days from the window's own Eastern date), so every layer, every hop and every node's outgoing edges sum to the same premium. Every layer is ranked by premium, largest at the top (rank numerals on the names), with the residual buckets last after a gap 1.6 times the normal one whatever their size (Other or Other names, then No sector, Sector unread, Sector pending; No expiry in the Expiry output). `mount(host)` draws v3 on Canvas 2D, laid out to `programme/NETWORK-DIRECTION.md`: money is the shape, a sphere's area is its premium (r = 6 + 28 sqrt(v / the largest node) px at 1440, never under 9) and a band's width is its premium (0.75 px per $1M, floor 1.25 px; the scale tightens as 56 px over the largest node so its bands never outgrow its sphere above a $75M node), one scale for every node and band and a legend row under the scene that draws three reference circles and three band swatches on that same scale; bands are filled Sankey bands stacked at each node in rank order so a node's outgoing widths add to its total, screen-blended in the lean colours (#2ee37a, #ff5a4e, #4ea2ff; Other and No sector in slate #6f7d99); spheres are lit sprites with a specular highlight and a rim, a halo that grows with premium, fog by depth and a soft shadow on a perspective floor grid; four glass planes stand behind the layers on a shallow arc. The scene is laid out in rest screen pixels (four columns at equal spacing centred on the midline, every stack centred with equal gaps, chips 22 px tall on one x edge per column, all four headers carrying the same total, controls above and the legend below, nothing else inside the scene) and lifted into world space with the inverse of the rest camera, so the symmetry holds to the pixel at rest and the sway (8 degrees over 40 s, pitch fixed at 11, reduced at layout to the widest amplitude at which no chip meets a sphere, a chip or a header, sampled at sixteen phases with the spheres at their 1.03 breathing maximum) supplies the depth. Below 640 px the layers become rows (ranks left to right, chips under their spheres in as many tiers as keep them apart) on a 0.62 scale; between 640 and 1100 px the scale is 0.85 or 0.72 and the chips two lines when one line would not clear the next column. Pulses travel every band from side to lean, one to four by premium and 7 s down to 2.4 s a lap, computed from the loop's clock with no per-frame allocation (batched by width into at most twenty strokes); spheres breathe 1.00 to 1.03 in rank-staggered phases; a window that arrives while the page is open flares its name (a 1.2 s ring) and lights its path for 1.5 s; hover, focus or a table row lights a subgraph and dims the rest, with a readout of the node's figure and share at the top right; Freeze stops the pulses, breathing, flares and sway (its label swaps to Resume and it carries no `aria-pressed`, so a screen reader hears one state; it is hidden under reduced motion, which draws one still frame). Below 640 px the four layer headers are drawn as dark chips with no band crossing them, and a hover readout always clears the headers. When the web font arrives after the first draw (`document.fonts.ready` and `loadingdone`, debounced to a frame and acted on only when the measured width of a reference string changed) the labels are measured again and the layout rebuilt, with keyboard focus kept. Under 540 px of module width the legend is two groups, each a title row over one row of three items, and the paths table rebalances its columns so no header truncates at 320 px. A pointer or horizontal touch drag orbits the camera (yaw within 55 degrees, 30 on a phone, pitch within 22, with inertia) but never past the angle at which a chip would meet a sphere, a chip or a header (`fits`, 6 bisections), so at 1440 it stops near 27 to 36 degrees; a double click or tap, R or 0 on a node, or Recentre returns it. The painter's order is floor, shadows, planes, bands, pulses, headers, spheres back to front, labels, and it stops when the tab is hidden or the canvas is off screen. `destroy()` cancels the loop, aborts the universe fetch, disconnects its observers and removes its listeners. The node hit targets (one roving tab stop after Freeze and Recentre, arrow keys between nodes, names linking to the ticker page), the canvas's spoken summary and the table of the 24 largest paths are its accessible half. It reads `/api/flows/universe` once for sectors and nothing else; the unusual controller hands it the alerts it already holds.

The flow network on the real unusual page in Chromium against `page.route` stubs, no server: layer counts and premium conservation through every layer, hop and node against an independent sum in Node, the ranking on screen at rest, at the reachable yaw and pitch limits, after reordering data and under reduced motion, contracts in the tooltips, mouse and touch orbit (clamps at the angle where a label would collide, inertia, recentring, a vertical touch still scrolling the page), hit targets after a rotation, the painter's order, hover, row and keyboard highlighting, the table and the canvas label, the freshness pill, the Expiry output, a flare on a new window, focus kept through a rebuild, pause when hidden or off screen, reduced motion, the pending, empty, failed and unread states, no overflow, no label or caption collision and every label within half a pitch of its own sphere at 320, 390, 700, 768, 1024, 1280 and 1440 px in both outputs over a 9 by 5 yaw and pitch grid, along sixteen points of the sway path and where a long drag stops, and the v3 audit (`auditFn`, run in the page on `net.scene()`) at rest at 1440, 1024 and 390 (columns or rows equally spaced within 1 px, every stack centred on the midline within 1 px, chips on one x edge per column, sphere radius, band width and each node's outgoing slice sum on the stated scale, the same total on every header, the legend's reference circles and swatches on that scale) and over a 0 to 40 s sweep at 0.1 s (no chip over a sphere or a chip, nothing outside the canvas); a readout and header clearance audit (a hover readout at least 12 px clear of every header and inside the canvas) and eight mutants of the served module (equal spheres, bands not by premium, unequal columns, an off-centre stack, a ragged chip edge, a header with another total, headers up under the readout, headers down on the spheres) that the audit must fail; a delayed-font block at 320 and 700 px (the woff2 held back 3 s, then labels, layout and collisions re-checked once it lands); at 320 and 390 px the legend's three circles on one row and its three swatches on one row, and no table header with a scrollWidth over its clientWidth; breathing between 1.00 and 1.03, Freeze, `destroy()` leaving no observer or listener of its own, no retained heap after 3,000 frames and under 3 KiB allocated a frame; CPU per frame at 120 or more bands and 200 pulses, also with the raster forced to finish (a pixel read after every draw), held as a ratio to a reference canvas workload timed in the same interleaved windows rather than as milliseconds, since an absolute figure flaked at load 10 on identical code (limit 2.5 times the reference, floor 12 ms; Generated documentation. `gen-docs.mjs` writes the File map, the course counts, the production globals and the suite lists in this file between their `gen:` markers, and `docs/index.md` (every tracked file with its role, its exports as `file#symbol`, and the suites that reach it), from `docs/modules.json` (one row per module: paths or globs, role, domain; a row with a `show` cell is also a File map line), `docs/globals.json`, `tests/suites.json` and the sources. `--check` exits 1 on drift. `docs-contract.mjs` fails on any difference, on a tracked file no row names and on a row that matches no file.

The reference audit: the share of `path:line` references in the listed documents (default `AGENTS.md`, `DEPLOY.md`, `README.md` and the frozen `docs/map-2026-10-05.md`) whose file is missing or whose line is past the end, printed, or written to the step summary when `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` is set. A report, not a gate.
